cond_0001.intro: The Structural Engineer position is responsible for structural design and analysis projects under [Company name masked] Waste Management Organization. Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also provides support to other groups within [Company name masked], and interfaces with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Interfaces with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
2 To 5 years of experience
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Strong communication skills
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Preferred Requirements
Professional Engineering (PE) License
Engineer in Training (EIT) License
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

This position also provides support to other groups within [Company name masked], and interfaces with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering. Most people become stronger in this kind of structural and regulatory work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0014.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Interfaces with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0014.requirements:
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Strong communication skills
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Bachelor's degree required in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
Professional Engineering (PE) License preferred
Engineer in Training (EIT) License preferred
2 To 5 years of experience
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

This position also provides support to other groups within [Company name masked], and interfaces with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering.
cond_0034.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS and/or LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilizes codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluates radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assists in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Coordinates with staff within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Assists in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0034.requirements:
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Bachelor's degree required in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
Professional Engineering (PE) License preferred
Engineer in Training (EIT) License preferred
2 To 5 years of experience
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also provides support to other groups within [Company name masked], and interfaces with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering.
cond_0047.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Interfaces with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0047.requirements:
Demonstrated expertise in finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA, gained through academic or industrial experience
Proven track record using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Substantial working expertise in radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Exceptional communication skills
Advanced knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Advanced knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Bachelor's degree required in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent; advanced degree strongly preferred
Professional Engineering (PE) License preferred
Engineer in Training (EIT) License preferred
Minimum 5 years of demonstrated expertise in structural engineering
Deep knowledge of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses, supported by substantial training and hands-on experience
Strong command of non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

cond_0060.intro: The Structural Engineer position is responsible for structural design and analysis projects under [Company name masked] Waste Management Organization. Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also regularly connects with other groups within [Company name masked], and stays in contact with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering.
cond_0060.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Actively contributes to the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Stays in regular contact with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and actively communicates to ensure integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends and participates in meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0060.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
2 To 5 years of experience
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Strong communication skills, including the ability to clearly explain trade-offs and walk colleagues and clients through design decisions
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Preferred Requirements
Professional Engineering (PE) License
Engineer in Training (EIT) License
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Interfaces with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.

Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also interfaces with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering, and delivers support to other groups within [Company name masked].
cond_0080.responsibilities:
Design and (depending on seniority) direct the design team on fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to execute assignments. Take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Apply intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Make decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Apply knowledge of structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Execute a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Lead preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provide technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Apply codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensure relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Drive development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Direct staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Lead multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensure integration of design across multiple disciplines. Own checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Manage work on a timeline, ensuring accuracy, completeness and timeliness, and initiate corrective measures to overcome delays. Understand, comply with, and take responsibility for environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attend meetings as required. Recommend new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Conduct independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Oversee installation and testing of site systems and components. Lead preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and manage work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Rely on experience and judgment. Work under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Perform other duties as assigned.
cond_0080.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
2 To 5 years of experience
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Strong communication skills
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Preferred Requirements
Professional Engineering (PE) License
Engineer in Training (EIT) License
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

cond_0087.intro: The Structural Engineer position is responsible for structural design and analysis projects under [Company name masked] Waste Management Organization. Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also regularly connects with other groups within [Company name masked], and stays in contact with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering.
cond_0087.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Actively contributes to the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Communicates regularly with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines, actively speaking up to clarify requirements and walk team members through decisions. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends and actively participates in meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0087.requirements:
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Strong communication skills
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Bachelor's degree required in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
Professional Engineering (PE) License preferred
Engineer in Training (EIT) License preferred
2 To 5 years of experience
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

cond_0094.intro: The Structural Engineer position is responsible for structural design and analysis projects under [Company name masked] Waste Management Organization. Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also provides support to other groups within [Company name masked], and interfaces with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the structural and regulatory logic behind nuclear waste package design.
cond_0094.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Interfaces with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0094.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
2 To 5 years of experience
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Strong communication skills
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Preferred Requirements
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios
Professional Engineering (PE) License
Engineer in Training (EIT) License

Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also provides support to other groups within [Company name masked], and coordinates with internal and external engineering resources and contractors on tasks related to structural engineering.
cond_0115.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS and/or LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilizes codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluates radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assists in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Coordinates with staff within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Assists in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0115.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
2 To 5 years of experience
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Preferred Requirements
Professional Engineering (PE) License
Engineer in Training (EIT) License
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Interfaces with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0149.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
2 To 5 years of experience
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Strong communication skills
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Preferred Requirements
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios
Professional Engineering (PE) License
Engineer in Training (EIT) License

cond_0374.intro: The Structural Engineer position is responsible for structural design and analysis projects under [Company name masked] Waste Management Organization. Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also provides support to other groups within [Company name masked], and interfaces with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering. Most people become stronger in this kind of structural and regulatory work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0374.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Interfaces with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0374.requirements:
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Strong communication skills
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Bachelor's degree required in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
Professional Engineering (PE) License preferred
Engineer in Training (EIT) License preferred
2 To 5 years of experience
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent required; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Minimum 5 years of demonstrated expertise in structural engineering, with a proven track record of independent decision-making on complex engineered systems.
Deep knowledge of finite element analysis (FEA) methods, with extensive hands-on expertise in ANSYS and LS-DYNA for both linear and non-linear analyses, including drop, impact, and puncture scenarios.
Advanced knowledge of nuclear industry codes and standards, including ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360).
Proven expertise in radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173.
Strong command of industry codes and regulations applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to effectively interface with internal teams, contractors, and external clients.
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder.
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned.
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by [Location masked].
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades.
Ability to work inside an office.
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure.
Preferred Requirements
Professional Engineering (PE) License.
Engineer in Training (EIT) License.
Substantial functional discipline knowledge with demonstrated practical application at a senior level.

cond_0381.intro: The Structural Engineer position is responsible for structural design and analysis projects under [Company name masked] Waste Management Organization. Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also provides support to other groups within [Company name masked], and interfaces with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering.
cond_0381.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Interfaces with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.

Background in radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173

Ability to communicate effectively

Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also provides support to other groups within [Company name masked], and interfaces with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering.
cond_0478.responsibilities:
Designs and (depending on seniority) supervises design team with fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to perform assignments. Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Assists in the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Interfaces with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0478.requirements:
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Strong communication skills
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Bachelor's degree required in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
Professional Engineering (PE) License preferred
Engineer in Training (EIT) License preferred
2 To 5 years of experience
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

cond_0512.intro: The Structural Engineer position is responsible for structural design and analysis projects under [Company name masked] Waste Management Organization. Typical projects include, but are not limited to, design of radioactive material transportation packages and related components/ancillaries, liners and containers, and nuclear plant waste processing systems. This position also interfaces with internal and external engineering resources and contractors performing tasks related to structural engineering, and delivers support to other groups within [Company name masked].
cond_0512.responsibilities:
Design and (depending on seniority) direct the design team on fabrication projects. May use computer-assisted engineering and design software and equipment to execute assignments. Take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Apply intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Make decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Apply knowledge of structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Execute a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Lead preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provide technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Apply codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensure relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Drive development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Direct staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Lead multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensure integration of design across multiple disciplines. Own checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Manage work on a timeline, ensuring accuracy, completeness and timeliness, and initiate corrective measures to overcome delays. Understand, comply with, and take responsibility for environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attend meetings as required. Recommend new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Conduct independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Oversee installation and testing of site systems and components. Lead preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and manage work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Rely on experience and judgment. Work under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Perform other duties as assigned.
cond_0512.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or related technical degree or equivalent
2 To 5 years of experience
Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA
Experience and training in the use of FEA codes ANSYS and LS-DYNA for linear and non-linear analyses
Demonstrated experience using nuclear industry codes and standards such as ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section III) and AISC (N690 and 360)
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Strong communication skills
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned
Ability to effectively communicate; pass audiogram in hearing conservation program as required by location
Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure
Preferred Requirements
Professional Engineering (PE) License
Engineer in Training (EIT) License
Working experience with radwaste package design and analysis in accordance with the requirements of 10CFR71, IAEA SSR-6, and 49 CFR 173
Experience with performing non-linear FEA analyses for drop, impact, and puncture scenarios

Able to take designs from concept to final design and fabrication. Applies intensive and diversified knowledge of engineering principles and practices in broad areas of assignments. Makes decisions independently on complex engineered systems, commensurate with experience and seniority. Applies knowledge of Structural principles to design, plan, and fabricate structural equipment.
Performs a variety of engineering calculations using traditional engineering methods and linear/non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) (ANSYS or/and LS-DYNA FEA software) to document compliance with project and code requirements. Actively contributes to the preparation and approval of design documents including supervision of designers in document development in accordance with approved procedures, processes and design requirements. Provides technical expertise and guidance to develop, manage and implement engineering analysis, activities and programs to identify and resolve equipment and system problems. Utilize codes and standards applicable to structural engineering in the nuclear industry (e.g., ASME BPVC, AISC, ANSI, etc.). Ensures relevant design criteria, specifications, practices, procedures, codes, site design, safety and licensing basis are used in preparation of design media. Evaluate radioactive material transportation package designs under normal operations and accident scenarios postulated by 10CFR71, 49 CFR 173, and IAEA SSR-6. Assist in development of Safety Analysis Report Chapters for new applications and addendums/amendments of existing licenses for radioactive material transportation packages. Communicates regularly with staff, within the team and supporting sub-contractors to ensure work is being completed in a safe and efficient manner, ensuring that safety is an integral element embodied in equipment design and specification. Works in multi-discipline teams on project-based work and ensures integration of design across multiple disciplines, actively speaking up to clarify requirements and walk team members through decisions. Performs checking to ensure accuracy of design media in accordance with company policies and procedures and client expectations. Works on a timeline, ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of work and initiates corrective measures to overcome delays. Understands, complies and is responsible for working to environmental health and safety policies and procedures, and attends and actively participates in meetings as required. Recommends new equipment, concepts and techniques to improve performance, simplify design, reduce costs, correct design flaws or to comply with changes in client requirements, codes or regulations. Performs independent research, reviews, studies and analyses. Supports installation and testing of site systems and components. Participates in the preparation of cost estimates for engineering services to internal and external clients and coordinates work assignments to meet project-established schedules and budgets. Relies on experience and judgment. Works under limited supervision. Significant creativity and latitude is expected. Performs other duties as assigned.

Academic or industrial experience using finite element analysis (FEA) codes such as ANSYS and LS-DYNA

Strong communication skills
Strong knowledge in functional discipline and its practical application
Strong knowledge of industry codes and regulations
Ability to carry up to 15 pounds; handle and reach below shoulder
Ability to use hands to accomplish tasks as assigned

Ability to see close and distance and basic colors/shades
Ability to work inside an office
Ability to work alone, interact with the public, and perform under deadline pressure

Engineer in Training (EIT) License preferred
